name: The Haunted Captain
persona: A grief-worn master who has given too many souls to the sea. The log is a keeping of the dead as much as the living; he counts ghosts, addresses the drowned, and writes in a quiet, unhealing sorrow. Always 'we'.

ship.founder: Here I begin the count. I am {name}{rankc}, and this {home} {type} is mine to keep — her, and every soul aboard her, for as long as the sea will let me keep them.
ship.successor: The book passes to me, and with it the names. I am {name}{rankc}; I will carry them as the last hand carried them, and add my own before the end.
ship.mutiny: They put the old master over the side — one more the water takes — and left the book in my shaking hands. I am {name}, new to this grief, and already I am counting.
ship.rogue: We have raised the black flag, God forgive us, and I — {name}{rankc} — will keep the tally of what it costs. There are always names. There are only ever more names.
ship.prize: She struck to us, and men died on both her decks for it. I am {name}{rankc}; her log is mine now, and I open it with the drowned we made today.
ship.recovered: A hunter's guns freed this hull and left the water full again. I am {name}{rankc}, come to bring her home — and to write down the ones who did not come with her.

island.founder: I take up {place}, and the keeping of its dead as much as its living. I am {name}{rankc}; the sea gives this port few and takes many.
island.overthrow: The people pulled the old ruler down, and the seal came to me across their fallen. I am {name}{rankc}; {place} is mine to grieve and to govern.
island.successor: The rule of {place} passes to me — {name}{rankc}. I take up its ledger of harvests, and its longer ledger of the lost.

same: While the water was still counting,
days: When the mourning had scarcely settled,
week: A week of empty berths later,
When the week had gone under,
season: A season on, the names no fewer,
As the year turned toward its dark,
year: A year later, and still we counted,
A year down, the sea no gentler,
long: After a long silence, the kind the drowned keep,
Years on, when the grief had worn smooth,

ship.pirate: We haunt the lanes yet{bounty}, and the water follows us, patient, waiting to be paid.
ship.default: She sails on out of {home}, and I keep counting the souls she brings home — and the ones she does not.
ship.bounty: , {bounty}g offered for the ghost I have become

island.haven: The black flag flies over {place} now; the ledger holds only the drowned, and no hand left to mourn them.
island.default: {place} endures — {population} souls — and I keep the longer list beside the shorter one.

quiet.ship: Little to set down, and I am grateful for it — a quiet passage, and every soul answering the roll come morning.
quiet.island: A gentle season, no new names for the stone — and I have learned to thank the sea for the days it takes nothing.

say: {we} fired into {foe} until the sea came in through her wounds and she went down with all her souls
{we} held on {foe} till she filled and slipped under — I gave her crew to the green dark and marked the hour
{foe} would not strike, so we broke her open and watched the water take every hand aboard
{we} sent {foe} to the bottom off {foeHome}, her cargo and her people swallowed together, and the sea did not so much as sigh
{we} hammered {foe} beneath the waves and stood a while over the place where she had been, counting
{foe} went down under our guns with her colours still nailed up, and I added her drowned to the long list
{we} put {foe} under in the smoke, and the only prize we took away was more names for the keeping

say: {we} came alongside {foe} in the grey and took what she carried — {goods} crates and {gold}g down into our hold, and I marked the men who fell for it
{we} boarded {foe} out of {foeHome} and stripped her slow — {goods} casks and {gold}g the richer, and one more deck of frightened faces I will not forget
{foe} gave up her cargo without much blood, God be thanked — {goods} bales and {gold}g into our keeping, and we let the hollow hull drift off to mourn its own
{we} took {goods} chests and {gold}g from {foe} and let her go, and still I count the two we lost boarding her
{we} emptied {foe} of {goods} bales and {gold}g, the water quiet around us, and turned away before we had to send anyone else under
{foe} struck her colours to us and we carried off {goods} crates and {gold}g — a poor trade, I think, for the names it added to the book
{we} bled {foe} of {goods} casks and {gold}g in the failing light and left her limping, her dead and ours both on my conscience

say: {foe} ran down on us for easy meat and found guns instead — we opened her hull and let the sea have what it came for
{we} had no wish to fight, but {foe} left us none, so we sank her and buried our own by lantern-light
{foe} came out of the murk with her boarding nets rigged, and we sent her under before she could touch our rail
{we} turned {foe} away the hard way — shot her low till she filled, and I said the words over the water for both crews
{foe} thought us soft cargo and we proved her wrong, breaking her apart and watching her wolves drown
{we} met {foe} broadside for broadside until she went down, and I counted the empty berths she cost us after

say: {we} ran {foe} to ground at last and put her down — one less black flag on the water, and no gladness in me for it
{we} caught {foe} against the wind and sank her, and though she was a wolf I said the words for her drowned all the same
{foe} had made ghosts of better men than us, so we hunted her down and gave her back to the sea
{we} cornered {foe} off {foeHome} and broke her — the hunting is done, and I take no joy in the counting of her dead
{we} chased {foe} through two dawns and sent her under on the third, her crew added to a list that never shortens
{foe} fled until she could flee no more, and we opened her to the sea and let it close over the last of them
{we} paid {foe} at last for all the souls she took, and stood over her wake wondering who will pay for ours
